question: What is the JUnit 5 test execution lifecycle?
title: JUnit 5 Test Lifecycle | Java Fresher Interview
direct_answer: For a simple Jupiter test class, **`@BeforeAll`** runs before its test invocations, then each invocation is surrounded by **`@BeforeEach`** and **`@AfterEach`**, and **`@AfterAll`** runs at the end. The default **PER_METHOD** lifecycle creates a new test instance for each test method or invocation. That isolates ordinary instance fields, but static fields, external systems, and other shared state can still couple tests.

sections.title: Quick revision
sections.content:
- **Order** — `@BeforeAll` → (per invocation: `@BeforeEach` → test → `@AfterEach`) → `@AfterAll`.
- **PER_METHOD default** — a fresh instance prevents ordinary instance fields from carrying over.
- **Shared state remains** — static fields, files, databases, and other external state still need isolation.
- **Class-level hooks** — normally static under PER_METHOD; PER_CLASS permits instance hooks.
- **Method order** — no source-order guarantee unless an orderer is configured.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
In a simple Jupiter class, `@BeforeAll` runs once before the test invocations. Under the default PER_METHOD lifecycle, Jupiter creates a new test instance for each method or parameterized invocation, runs `@BeforeEach`, runs the test, and then runs `@AfterEach`. After the invocations finish, `@AfterAll` runs once.

The fresh instance prevents ordinary instance fields from carrying values into the next test, which is why class-level hooks are normally static under PER_METHOD. It does not isolate static fields, a database, files, or other external state. With `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)`, one instance is reused and class-level hooks may be instance methods, so mutable fields need deliberate reset. Test method order is separate and should not be assumed from source order.

sections.title: How one class-level lifecycle contains repeated test cycles
sections.content:
JUnit begins the class lifecycle with **`@BeforeAll`** and ends it with **`@AfterAll`**. Between those hooks, every test invocation has its own cycle: JUnit creates the test instance under the default `PER_METHOD` mode, runs **`@BeforeEach`**, runs the test, and then runs **`@AfterEach`**.

For example, a class with two `@Test` methods runs the before-each and after-each hooks twice, but the before-all and after-all hooks once. The fresh instance prevents ordinary instance fields from leaking state between tests. Class-level lifecycle methods are therefore static by default. `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` permits non-static class-level hooks, but it also reuses one instance, so mutable fields must be reset deliberately. Test correctness must never depend on method order.

sections.title: Lifecycle Order
sections.content:
```mermaid flowchart TB A["@BeforeAll (static)
once per class"] --> B["new test instance"] B --> C["@BeforeEach"] C --> D["@Test method"] D --> E["@AfterEach"] E --> F{"more tests?"} F -->|yes| B F -->|no| G["@AfterAll (static)
once per class"] ```

sections.title: Observing the Order
Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- **Assuming one shared instance.** Under the default lifecycle each test method or invocation gets a new instance; static fields and external systems can still carry state.
- **`@BeforeAll` before each test.** It runs once for the container, not per invocation — that is `@BeforeEach`.
- **Non-static `@BeforeAll` under `PER_METHOD`.** Jupiter rejects the lifecycle method unless it is static; `PER_CLASS` permits an instance method.
- **Relying on source order.** Test order is controlled only when an explicit orderer is configured, and ordinary tests should not depend on one another.

beats.text: JUnit 5's default lifecycle is PER_METHOD: a new test class instance is created before every @Test method. The full order is @BeforeAll once, then for every test: @BeforeEach, @Test, @AfterEach, and finally @AfterAll once at the end.
A fresh instance prevents ordinary instance fields from carrying over. Static fields, databases, files, caches, and other external state can still couple tests and need their own isolation.

items: @BeforeAll: static, runs once before any test in the class
@BeforeEach: runs before each @Test — fresh setup per test
@AfterAll: static, runs once after all tests in the class

beats.text: Under the default `PER_METHOD` lifecycle, class-level callbacks are static. With `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)`, JUnit reuses one test instance and permits instance `@BeforeAll`/`@AfterAll` methods. That can help with instance-managed resources, but mutable fields are then shared and must be handled deliberately.

items: Using a non-static @BeforeAll in the default PER_METHOD lifecycle — Jupiter reports an invalid lifecycle method unless PER_CLASS is selected
Assuming PER_METHOD isolates static or external state; it resets only the test instance

speakable_v2.cap: PER_METHOD isolates ordinary instance fields by default; the test suite must still control every shared resource and external state.
